age_band.note: The view of the ridge is the reward of the Sulphur Skyline trail: 8.8 km return with 700 m of climbing (Parks Canada). No source gives an age.

suitability.kid_note: Ashlar Ridge is seen, not climbed: the Sulphur Skyline trail from the Miette Hot Springs car park looks across to it after a steep 700 m climb. The road to Miette is closed from mid-October to mid-May.

stroller.note: A steep mountain trail all the way to the top (Parks Canada).

wheelchair.note: A steep mountain trail; the accessible facilities page lists no access to the Sulphur Skyline.

on_site_min.quote: Sulphur Skyline 8.8 km return; elevation gain/loss: 700 m; 4-6 hrs

exposure.note: An alpine summit trail; no railings are described.

walk_m.note: Half of the 8.8 km return trail from the Miette Hot Springs parking lot to the viewpoint summit.

v.note: Miette Road is closed to vehicles from mid-October to mid-May; the trail is usually snow free by late May

age_band.note: The Toe of the Athabasca Glacier trail is 1.8 km return with 60 m of climbing; no age limit to look at the glacier.

suitability.kid_note: Stay behind the barriers: Parks Canada warns that people have died in hidden crevasses. The short Toe of the Glacier trail starts at the end of the gravel Glacier Road across from the Icefield Centre.

stroller.note: The lower lot is heavily rutted gravel and the trail crosses rock; the accessible facilities page names no accessible route to the toe.

wheelchair.quote: two designated accessible stalls (no side access aisle) in the heavily rutted, lower parking area
wheelchair.note: The glacier can be seen from the lower parking area; the trail itself is not accessible.

on_site_min.quote: Toe of the Athabasca Glacier 1.8 km return; elevation gain/loss: 60 m; 1 hr
on_site_min.note: The upper bound is our margin for the view.

v.where: the glacier toe beyond the barriers: crevasses and collapsing ice

exposure.quote: Caution - The glacier is dangerous! For your safety do not cross the barriers.

walk_m.quote: Toe of the Athabasca Glacier 1.8 km return
walk_m.note: Half of the 1.8 km return trail from the trailhead lot.

v.note: Icefields Parkway: no seasonal closure stated; check road conditions in winter

access_season.note: The hiking guide lists the trail without a season; the Glacier Road lot is reached from Highway 93N.

v.note: Hidden crevasses and collapsing ice at the toe; do not cross the barriers

suitability.kid_note: The 1928 boathouse stands on the shore beside the Maligne Lake car parks. Canoe and kayak rentals from it are not open to anyone under 18, and under-16s must be with a parent or guardian.

stroller.note: The first 300 m of the Mary Schäffer Loop along the shore near the boathouse are paved (accessible facilities page).

wheelchair.quote: The first 300 m of the Mary Shäffer Loop is paved with gorgeous lake and mountain views.
wheelchair.note: Accessible stalls and toilets at the lake; the public docks have a high step.

on_site_min.note: Our estimate: a look at the boathouse, or one to two hours with a rental.

age_band.note: Lakeshore walks start at the car parks; the Mary Schäffer Loop is 2.9 km with no climbing.

suitability.kid_note: Spirit Island is 14 km up the lake with no road or trail: only tour boats and paddlers reach it. From the car parks the paved start of the Mary Schäffer Loop follows the shore.

stroller.quote: The first 300 m of the Mary Shäffer Loop is paved with gorgeous lake and mountain views.

wheelchair.note: Accessible stalls in the main and dock lots, an accessible toilet stall, 300 m of paved path; docks have a high step.

on_site_min.quote: Mary Schäffer Loop 2.9 km loop; no elevation gain; 1-2 hrs

walk_m.note: The trail starts at the first parking lot and goes down to the shore; 50 m is our estimate.

v.note: Maligne Lake Road; the Maligne Canyon area stays closed for 2026

access_season.note: The lake page describes year-round use (skiing in winter); Maligne Canyon, on the same road, is closed for 2026.

v.note: Moose and bears use the forest at the north end of the lake
Cold glacial water; Spirit Island is 14 km up the lake

age_band.note: The north face is seen from the parking area; the paved Path of the Glacier climbs steeply for 800 m.

suitability.kid_note: Cavell Road is closed for all of 2026. When it is open, the north face and Angel Glacier are seen from the car park, and a steep paved path climbs 800 m to the meltwater lake. Vehicles over 25 feet are not allowed on the road.

stroller.note: The Path of the Glacier is paved but very steep for its first part.

wheelchair.quote: Nothing can prepare you for the awesome size and sheerness of the mountain’s north face as seen from the parking area.
wheelchair.note: Accessible stalls in the upper lot; the paved trail is very steep.

on_site_min.note: Our estimate for the view and the Path of the Glacier; no time is published.

exposure.note: Viewpoints on moraine; fencing is not described.

walk_m.quote: The paved Path of the Glacier Trail climbs very steeply from the parking area before leveling out 800 m up the trail

v.note: Cavell Road closed for the 2026 season

access_season.note: Outside 2026 the road also closes 1 November to 15 May for caribou.

age_band.note: Seen from the paved path at Athabasca Falls; no age limit.

suitability.kid_note: The mountain is the backdrop of Athabasca Falls: the paved path from the falls car park gives the view. Keep children behind the railings; the mist makes the rock slippery.

stroller.note: A paved path, though with steep and uneven sections and 14 steps to the bridge.

wheelchair.quote: A paved path provides a beautiful view of Mount Kerkeslin and the Athabasca River at the top of these thundering falls.

on_site_min.note: Our estimate for the view from the falls path.

exposure.quote: For your own safety, do not cross the railings.

walk_m.quote: The 150 m path to the falls’ upper viewpoint has steep and uneven sections.
